title: The Medical Emergency notice on the public QR page is white text on a pale pink panel (1.09:1) — unreadable in BOTH light and dark

Add a unit test asserting no `text-white` appears inside an `Alert` whose container is a `-50` tint.

title: Systemic root cause: the whole leaf/mint/officer surface family has no dark value at all — 20 tokens are declared in :root and never redefined under .dark, and 695 hardcoded light-surface classes sit under themed text
evidence: Diffed the two blocks programmatically: :root declares 57 custom properties, `.dark` redefines 34, and 23 are never redefined — including every surface token the redesign is built on: --leaf, --leaf-300/600/700/800, --leaf-soft, --leaf-ring, --lime, --lime-soft, --mint-bg, --mint-soft, --avatar-bg, --officer-700/800/soft, plus --success/--warning/--info. Grep over src for opaque light-surface classes (bg-white, bg-slate-50/100/200, bg-leaf-soft, bg-mint-*, bg-officer-soft, bg-gray-50/100, bg-{red,blue,green,amber}-50, excluding /alpha overlays and __tests__): 748 occurrences, 695 (93%) carry no `dark:` variant on the line, and 309 of those also carry no hardcoded text colour, so their text falls back to --foreground (#f2f2f2 in dark). Extreme case: /accessibility and /help/faq are byte-identical between dark and light (md5 of accessibility__w1440__dark.png == __light.png; same for help_faq__w1440) because faq-client.tsx and page.tsx are 100% hardcoded slate/white. Second live instance of the exact `.gov-auth-input` bug (banked finding A) at globals-components-layout.css:116-124: `.field-emphasis { background: #fff !important; color: hsl(var(--foreground)); }` — 7 in-app fields.
why_it_matters: Findings A and B are not two bugs, they are two samples of one: text colour flips through CSS variables, surface colour does not. Every fix applied one call site at a time will be undone by the next feature that types `bg-white`. Until the tokens exist there is nothing a developer can correctly reach for, and dark mode cannot be trusted on any screen that has not been individually screenshotted.
fix: Add the missing surface values to the `.dark` block in globals.css (after line 150), keeping the token names so no call site changes: `--leaf-soft: 153 25% 14%; --leaf-700: #4ec988; --leaf-800: #6fd9a0; --mint-bg: 150 18% 8%; --mint-soft: 150 16% 11%; --officer-soft: 190 25% 14%; --officer-700: #5fc5d3; --lime-soft: 70 25% 14%; --avatar-bg: 150 25% 20%; --leaf-ring: rgba(110,220,160,0.20);` (the -700/-800 pair inverts role in dark: on a dark ground the readable green must be light). Then make the Tailwind tokens read the variables instead of literal hexes — in tailwind.config.cjs:80-110 change `soft: '#eaf9f0'` to `soft: 'hsl(var(--leaf-soft))'` etc., so `bg-leaf-soft` flips automatically at all 204 call sites. Finally add a lint rule banning bare `bg-white`/`bg-slate-{50,100,200}` in src/app and src/components (allow-list `dark:` pairs and the QR quiet-zone at (public)/verify/[cert-number]/page.tsx:275 which deliberately uses `dark:bg-white`).

title: The language toggle on the accessibility statement is white-on-white (1.03:1) — invisible on the one page that promises WCAG AA
evidence: report__w1440__light.json, report__w1440__dark.json and report__w390__light.json all report the identical violation on /accessibility: `.gap-1` — 'insufficient color contrast of 1.03 (foreground #fefefe, background #f8fafc, font size 8.3pt (11px))'. Opened accessibility__w1440__dark.png: at the top-right of the document, level with the ฉบับร่าง line, there is a faint ghost where a control should be — no visible EN/TH label. Source: LanguageToggle's default `topbar` variant hardcodes `text-white/80` (line 187) and its label span is `flex items-center gap-1 … text-[11px]` (line 191) — the exact axe target. The variant was designed to sit on the dark-green `.gov-topbar` gradient; client-view.tsx:52 renders it bare inside `prose prose-slate` on the slate-50 page.
why_it_matters: §3 of this very statement claims 'รองรับการสลับภาษาไทยและภาษาอังกฤษ' and §2 claims WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. The control that makes the first claim true is invisible, and it fails the second claim by a factor of four. An English-speaking reader — the audience this page's English mode exists for — cannot find the switch. It is the one page where a contrast failure is also a credibility failure.
fix: Two lines. LanguageToggle.tsx:187 — make the topbar variant's colour contextual instead of assumed: `text-white/80 … hover:text-white` → `text-[color:var(--toggle-fg,theme(colors.white/0.8))] … hover:text-[color:var(--toggle-fg-strong,#fff)]`, and set `--toggle-fg` on `.gov-topbar`. Simpler and safer for today: in accessibility/client-view.tsx:52 pass the variant that was built for a light ground — `<LanguageToggle variant="pill" className="!bg-muted !text-foreground" />` — and add a regression test asserting the toggle's computed colour differs from its parent background on this route.

title: Dark mode has no CSS `color-scheme` — the app sets an inert `data-color-scheme` attribute instead, so 38 native selects, date pickers and Chrome autofill stay light
where: apps/web-app/src/components/theme/theme-script.tsx:15,18 · theme-provider.tsx:19 · components/layout/dashboard-layout.tsx:190 · no CSS `color-scheme` declaration anywhere in src
evidence: Grepped `color-scheme` across all .css/.tsx/.ts in apps/web-app/src: every hit is `setAttribute('data-color-scheme', …)` — a custom data attribute with zero rendering effect. The CSS property `color-scheme: dark` is never declared in globals.css, globals-components-auth.css, globals-components-layout.css, globals-premium.css or provider-styles.css. `<select>` appears 38 times in src (excluding tests). Combined with globals-components-auth.css:277-279 (`.gov-auth-input { background: #fff !important }`), the login ID field is the exact surface Chrome repaints on autofill with its own light-mode background and text colour.
why_it_matters: Three separate code paths carefully set an attribute that does nothing, which is worse than omitting it: it looks like the fix is in place. The visible cost is that every dropdown popup, date picker and autofill highlight in a dark session opens as a light-mode UA widget — and on the login page, autofill lands on the one field where text is already invisible (banked finding A), so a returning farmer's saved ID may render as a white-on-white block.
fix: Add to globals.css inside @layer base: `:root { color-scheme: light; }` and `.dark { color-scheme: dark; }`. Keep the data attribute if tests select on it, but the CSS property is what the browser reads. Then remove the `!important` white from `.gov-auth-input` (globals-components-auth.css:278) — `background: hsl(var(--card))` — which fixes banked finding A across all 11 `.gov-auth-input` fields in 4 files (login, provider login, register, forgot-password) in one line, and add `input:-webkit-autofill { -webkit-text-fill-color: hsl(var(--foreground)); -webkit-box-shadow: 0 0 0 1000px hsl(var(--card)) inset; }`.

title: Switching theme is a three-speed staggered flip: surfaces and body text snap instantly while buttons, links and inputs cross-fade at 150ms, 200ms and 250ms
evidence: theme-provider.tsx:42 flips the class with `classList.toggle('dark', …)` and nothing else. Grepped every transition declaration in the four stylesheets: there is no `transition` on `html`, `body`, or any surface rule — body (globals.css:442) and html (globals.css:464) declare none. But globals.css:296-301 applies `transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow, opacity; transition-duration: 150ms` to `a, button, [role="button"], input, select, textarea`, while `.gov-auth-input` uses `all 200ms` (auth.css:284), `.gov-auth-primary-btn` `all 250ms` (auth.css:321), `.gov-auth-link` `color 200ms` (auth.css:382) and `.gov-bottom-nav-item` `200ms` (layout.css:312).
why_it_matters: The page ground and every heading change in frame one, then the controls catch up in three different waves. On the login screen the white input slabs are still white for 200ms after the panel behind them has gone black. This is not 'no transition' — it is a visibly wrong one, and it is the moment a user judges whether the product was built with care. The fix is also the cheapest polish available on the whole platform.
fix: Add a single coordinated cross-fade and let reduced-motion opt out (the guard at globals.css:321-331 already covers it): `html.theme-transition, html.theme-transition *, html.theme-transition *::before, html.theme-transition *::after { transition: background-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) !important; }`. In theme-provider.tsx:41-44 (and the duplicate at dashboard-layout.tsx:186-192) add the class before toggling `dark` and remove it on a 260ms timeout, so the class is only present during the flip and never slows normal hover states.

title: Secondary links fail AA on all three auth doors in dark (3.21:1) — including 'ลืมรหัสผ่าน?', the link a locked-out farmer needs most
evidence: report__w1440__dark.json flags the same violation on three routes: /login and /auth/health/login `a[href$="forgot-password"]` and /register `.mb-6` — 'insufficient color contrast of 3.21 (foreground #1d724c, background #0c120f, font size 9.8pt (13px), font weight bold)'. Confirmed by eye in login__w1440__dark.png: 'ลืมรหัสผ่าน?', 'สมัครสมาชิก' and 'สำหรับเจ้าหน้าที่' render as murky dark green against the near-black panel. Source: `.gov-auth-link { color: hsl(153 60% 28%) }` with a comment at :378-379 explaining the value was tuned for the #f4f6f5 LIGHT form panel — there is no `.dark` counterpart, consistent with the token audit in finding 3 (--leaf-700/800 absent from `.dark`).

The affected links are account recovery, registration and the officer door: the three exits from a login screen. A user who cannot log in and cannot see the recovery link has no path forward, and this platform's users are farmers on phones in daylight.

Same treatment for `.gov-auth-alert-danger`/`-success` (auth.css:410-420), which hardcode `hsl(0 80% 97%)` and `hsl(142 72% 96%)` fills that stay bright white-pink and white-green on a black page.

title: The dark theme is an inversion, not a designed palette: 16.9:1 body glare, brand hue stripped from the ink, and elevation carried by a 6/255 luminance step with shadows that cannot render
evidence: Computed from the declared tokens and confirmed against report__w1440__dark.json metrics (bodyBg rgb(12,18,15), bodyColor rgb(242,242,242) on every dark route): body contrast is 16.91:1, versus 13.92:1 for Material's reference dark body treatment (#DEDEDE on #121212). Light mode's ink is brand-tinted — `--foreground: 150 30% 8%` on `--background: 150 12% 96%` — but dark mode's ink is `--foreground: 0 0% 95%`, zero saturation: the green comes out of the type entirely. Elevation: `--card: 150 20% 9%` = rgb(18,28,23) on `--background: 150 20% 6%` = rgb(12,18,15), a 6-unit RGB step, and the only other elevation cue is `--shadow-sm/-md: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)` (globals.css:149-150) — a black shadow that cannot darken a near-black ground. Visible in pricing__w1440__dark.png: the two fee cards read as one continuous slab, and the navy footer (`bg-gov-navy` #0b1f3a, Footer.tsx:125, never themed) is brighter than the page above it, so the page darkens as you scroll then abruptly turns blue.
why_it_matters: Dark mode exists to be gentler at night; at 16.9:1 with pure-white input slabs (#fff on #0c120f = 18.94:1, visible as two glowing rectangles in login__w1440__dark.png) it is harsher than the light theme. Meanwhile the brand disappears — a Thai government platform whose identity is deep forest green renders its dark theme in neutral grey on green-black, with a navy footer from a fourth palette bolted on. It reads as machine-inverted rather than designed.
fix: In globals.css `.dark` (line 114): soften and re-tint the ink — `--foreground: 150 8% 90%;` (13.9:1, carries a trace of the brand hue) and `--muted-foreground: 150 8% 66%`. Open the elevation gap so surfaces are distinguishable without shadow — `--background: 150 20% 5%; --card: 150 16% 12%; --popover: 150 16% 14%;` — and replace the useless black shadows with a light rim: `--shadow-sm: 0 0 0 1px hsl(150 15% 22%); --shadow-md: 0 8px 24px -12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.8), 0 0 0 1px hsl(150 15% 22%);`. Give the footer a dark value so it stops being the brightest band on the page: Footer.tsx:125 `bg-gov-navy` → `bg-gov-navy dark:bg-[#060d18]`.

title: Three independent theme-toggle implementations; the dashboard one bypasses the provider, so the settings switch shows the wrong position until reload
evidence: AppThemeProvider is mounted once at app root (providers.tsx:11) and reads localStorage in a mount-only effect (theme-provider.tsx:59-70); it registers no `storage` listener. login-chooser.tsx:310 and health/settings/client-view.tsx:32 both drive theme through that context. dashboard-layout.tsx:186-192 does not: it calls `localStorage.setItem` + `document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', …)` directly and dispatches `new Event('storage')` — a bare Event with no `key`, which the provider does not listen for in any case. So after a user toggles from the dashboard topbar, the provider's `colorScheme` state is stale for the rest of the SPA session.
why_it_matters: Concretely: a farmer in light mode taps the moon in the dashboard topbar (page goes dark), then opens /health/settings — the dark-mode switch renders in the OFF position on a dark page, and the first tap sets 'dark' again, so nothing happens. They must tap twice to get back to light. Separately, /auth is the only public page with a toggle at all (grep for `useAppTheme` returns exactly two files: the provider and login-chooser), so a signed-out visitor who turns dark on has no control anywhere else on the public site to turn it off.
fix: Delete the duplicate implementation. In dashboard-layout.tsx replace the local `isDark` state and `toggleTheme` (lines 115, 121-122, 186-192) with `const { colorScheme, toggleColorScheme } = useAppTheme()` — the provider already persists and applies. Then add the same toggle to the public GovLayout header so /pricing, /about, /help, /verify and /trace can leave dark mode. As a safety net, give AppThemeProvider a `storage` listener mirroring the one in language-context.tsx:30-47 so any future direct writer stays in sync.

title: The palette is an accumulation, not a system: six green families defined, two carry 97% of the traffic, one has zero call sites and the legacy Mantine set costs 91 tokens for 37 references
evidence: Counted utility references across src (.tsx, excluding __tests__): leaf 870, primary- 242, teal- 27, green- 25, emerald- 5, mantine-green 5, gov-green 3, mantine-teal 2, and `brand-*` — 10 shades declared at tailwind.config.cjs:111-121 — returns 0 matches anywhere in src across .tsx/.ts/.css. All Mantine colour utilities together total 37 references, against a palette of 10 families × ~10 shades declared at :152-163. globals.css:469-475 declares six `.status-*` badge classes; grep for all six across src returns 0 call sites — dead CSS, one of which (`.status-approved`) would compute to 2.80:1 in dark if anything did use it.
why_it_matters: An engineer choosing a green today has six plausible answers and no rule that picks one, so the next screen adds a seventh variant rather than reusing the sixth. That is exactly how findings 1-6 arose: when there is no obvious token, `bg-white` is the honest default. The config's own comments admit it — 'DO NOT add new references — migrate' (line 149) and 'Removal: Wave F' — but the wave never landed, so the warning has become part of the furniture. The cost is not bytes, it is that no one can tell which green is correct.
fix: Three deletions, all zero-risk and independently verifiable. (1) Delete the `brand` block (tailwind.config.cjs:111-121) — 0 call sites; re-run the grep after to prove it. (2) Delete the six `.status-*` rules (globals.css:469-475) — 0 call sites. (3) Reduce `mantine` to only the shades still referenced by the 37 remaining call sites (a script over the grep output gives the exact list — likely under 15 entries), and add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule that errors on any NEW `-mantine-` class so the count can only fall. Then write the one-paragraph rule the palette lacks and put it at the top of tailwind.config.cjs: `primary` = deep forest, text/depth/links/gov chrome; `leaf` = action and surface; `officer` = the staff door only; `gov` = fixed print/letterhead artefacts that must not follow the theme.

title: Two-line Thai hero headings on every auth page overlap: the line box is 51px but the ink band is 54px
evidence: CSS at :133-137 is `font-size: 2.85rem; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1.12; letter-spacing: -0.02em`. 2.85rem = 45.6px, so the line box is 45.6 × 1.12 = 51.07px. title: Thai compound words break across lines mid-word — confirmed on /auth and /health/payments
evidence: Confirmed the suspected break. In /home/ubuntu/.claude/jobs/187183e9/tmp/qa/shots/auth__w1440__light.png, cropped at 3x (/tmp/c_auth_sub.png), the subtitle's line 1 ends '…ติดตามสถานะ ชำระค่า' and line 2 begins 'ธรรมเนียม' — 'ค่าธรรมเนียม' (fee) is split. title: The brand font's two dominant weights are never preloaded — 1,245 semibold/medium strings paint in the fallback first
evidence: layout.tsx preloads exactly two faces: /fonts/SukhumvitSet-Text.ttf (400) and /fonts/SukhumvitSet-Bold.ttf (700), with the comment at :88-92 stating the intent is 'so the first paint doesn't flash the Sarabun fallback'. The two most-used weights after bold — 600 (743) and 500 (502), 1,245 combined — map to SukhumvitSet-SemiBold.ttf and SukhumvitSet-Medium.ttf (declared @font-face in src/styles/globals.css:16-17, `font-display: swap`), neither of which is preloaded. The fallback they swap from is Sarabun, and layout.tsx:22-23 loads only Sarabun 400 and 700 — so a 600 request against the fallback snaps to 700.

Separately, convert all six faces to woff2 (`pyftsubset` or `woff2_compress`), update the six @font-face src URLs in globals.css:14-22 and the four preloads to `type="font/woff2"` — that cuts the four preloaded faces from ~341KB to roughly 150KB and removes most of the swap window.

title: Thai and Arabic numerals mixed inside one legal document, including a WCAG ratio written as ๔.๕ ต่อ ๑
evidence: :34 reads 'สีพื้นกับสีตัวอักษรผ่านเกณฑ์ WCAG ระดับ AA (อย่างน้อย ๔.๕ ต่อ ๑ สำหรับข้อความปกติ)' — the contrast ratio 4.5:1 in Thai numerals, in the same sentence as the Arabic-numeral standard name. :51 reads '…ภายใน ๑๕ วันทำการ … ภายใน ๖๐ วัน … ทุก ๓๐ วัน'. title: Two glyphs used 333 times in the UI do not exist in the brand font and silently render from a system fallback
where: App-wide; most visible at /health/payments 390px — /home/ubuntu/work/GACP-Certification-Application/apps/web-app/src/app/health/payments/client-view.tsx:575. Font files: apps/web-app/public/fonts/SukhumvitSet-*.ttf

title: An unlayered stylesheet loaded after @tailwind utilities makes every padding/radius utility on every form field silently dead — the search icon prints on top of the placeholder at both viewports
where: All form fields platform-wide. Root: apps/web-app/src/styles/globals-components-layout.css:116-124 + apps/web-app/src/app/globals.css:3. Visible symptom: /health/applications — apps/web-app/src/components/feature/filter-bar.tsx:38-43; latent in apps/web-app/src/components/ui/primitives/input.tsx:37
evidence: app/globals.css imports styles/globals.css (which emits `@tailwind base/components/utilities` at lines 1-3) FIRST, then imports globals-components-layout.css at line 3. That file has no `@layer` wrapper (grep for @layer in it returns nothing), so its `.field-emphasis { padding: 0.625rem 1rem; }` at line 119 sits after every Tailwind utility at equal specificity and wins every tie. filter-bar.tsx:38 absolutely positions a `<Search className="absolute left-3 h-4 w-4">` (occupying x 12-28px) and passes `className="pl-10"` at line 43 to compensate — that utility is overridden, so the text starts at 16px. I opened health_applications__w1440__light.png and health_applications__w390__light.png: in BOTH, the magnifier glyph is drawn on top of the first characters of 'ค้นหาด้วยเลขคำขอ ชื่อฟาร์ม หรือชื่อพืช', which renders as '(icon)นหาด้วยเลขคำขอ…'. The same dead-utility mechanism applies to input.tsx:37's own `showSection && 'pl-9'`, i.e. every Input using the leftSection/icon API. The same rule's `background: #fff !important` at line 118 is the mechanism behind banked finding A (dark-mode input on a white ground) and `border-radius: 0.75rem !important` at line 117 is why no input can ever match a card's radius.
why_it_matters: This is one line of CSS quietly disabling an entire category of layout control across the platform, and it is why the same bug keeps reappearing in different clothes — dead padding here, a white field in dark mode there, a radius that refuses to change. Every future fix that reaches for a Tailwind utility on a field will fail for reasons nobody can see in the JSX.
fix:
Two steps. (1) Put the file inside the cascade layer it belongs to so utilities win again — in globals-components-layout.css wrap the whole file: `@layer components { … }`, and drop the three `!important` flags on lines 117, 118 and 122 (theme-reactive tokens should carry those values: `background: hsl(var(--card))` not `#fff !important`). (2) In the meantime, stop the visible collision by using the primitive's own API instead of a hand-placed icon — filter-bar.tsx:37-44 becomes: -
- - -
+
+ } /> +
and change input.tsx:37 from the utility `'pl-9'` to an inline style or a layered rule that can actually beat .field-emphasis until step (1) lands.

title: Loading placeholders are shaped nothing like the content they stand in for — the whole page jumps when the fetch resolves (CLS 0.115 profile, 0.19 trace, 0.060 workspaces)
evidence: Measured CLS from the reports: /health/profile 0.1149 and /health/profile/security 0.0765 and /health/workspaces 0.0602 (shots-auth/report__w1440__light.json); /trace/<qr> 0.161 desktop / 0.1915 mobile (shots/report__w1440__light.json, report__w390__light.json). Causes read in source: (a) profile-client.tsx:101 returns `<PageSkeleton type="form" />`, which page-skeleton.tsx:172-194 renders as ONE card containing a title bar, four label+42px field rows and a button row; the content it is standing in for — visible in health_profile__w1440__light.png — is a SummaryHeader, a green identity banner, a four-row info card and six navigation rows, running y=88 to y=1360. Everything below moves when the swap happens. (b) trace/[qr-code]/client-view.tsx:71-80 renders `<div className="flex h-screen items-center justify-center bg-slate-50">` with a centred spinner, then replaces the entire document with a ~2000px green-hero page — with loadMs 6579 on mobile, that full-document swap is the whole 0.19. imgCount is 0 for that route, so no image is involved; it is purely unreserved late-mounted content. (c) workspaces/page.tsx:170 gates an invitations banner on `!invitationsLoading && invitations.length > 0` and inserts it ABOVE the workspace list, while :152-153 conditionally appends a fifth stat chip to the header after the same fetch — two unreserved insertions above existing content.
why_it_matters: 0.1149 and 0.1915 are both over Google's 0.1 'good' CLS threshold, and CLS is not an abstract score here: on the trace page a buyer who starts reading at second 4 has the whole page yanked out from under them at second 6.5. A skeleton that does not match its content is worse than no skeleton — it promises a shape and then breaks the promise.
fix:
(a) Give profile its own skeleton whose blocks match its real blocks, not a generic 'form': add `type="profile"` to PageSkeleton rendering header 130px + banner 130px + info card 410px + six 76px rows, or simpler — render the real SummaryHeader immediately (its text is static) and skeletonise only the four data rows. (b) In trace/[qr-code]/client-view.tsx:71-80, stop replacing the document: keep the hero and the card frames mounted and put the spinner inside the product card only, so the page's outline never moves: `if (loading) return
;` (c) In workspaces/page.tsx, render the invitations region unconditionally with `min-h-0` reserved space while `invitationsLoading`, and keep the stats array length constant by rendering the คำเชิญรอตอบรับ chip always with value 0 rather than appending it at :152-153.

title: The finance Document Lifecycle stepper is broken at both ends: three islands in a 400px void at 1440, and the third document clipped off-screen with the scrollbar hidden by a class that does not exist at 390
evidence: Opened health_payments__w1440__light.png: chip 1 sits at x=103-186, its chevron at x=207, then 418px of empty card before chip 2 at x=625, its chevron at x=766, then 417px of nothing before chip 3 at x=1183. The arrow points at emptiness. Cause is line 554 `sm:justify-between` applied to wrappers that each bundle [chip + chevron] together (line 560 `<div className="flex shrink-0 items-center">` containing both the chip and, at 568-570, the chevron), so justify-between distributes the bundles and the connector travels with the left chip instead of centring in the gap. Opened health_payments__w390__light.png: the third chip is cut at the card's right edge, reading 'ใบเสร็จรับเงิน /' and 'Receipt / Tax In', with no fade, no arrow and no scrollbar. The `no-scrollbar` class on line 554 that hides the only affordance is defined NOWHERE — grep across src/**/*.css, tailwind.config.cjs and postcss.config.cjs returns nothing, and the only registered Tailwind plugin is @tailwindcss/typography (tailwind.config.cjs:206). The same dead class is used on app/health/planting/client-view.tsx:117 and app/health/applications/new/_steps/layout.tsx:170 — the wizard step indicator.
why_it_matters: The comment at lines 540-553 explains at length that this strip must show exactly three documents because a farmer who miscounts waits for a paper that does not exist. The layout then hides the third one on a phone. And the desktop rendering makes a three-step process read as three unrelated tiles rather than a sequence.
fix:
Flatten the row so the chevrons are siblings, then centre instead of spreading. Line 554-572:
- <div className="no-scrollbar -mx-4 flex items-center overflow-x-auto px-4 sm:mx-0 sm:justify-between sm:overflow-visible sm:px-0">
+ <div className="-mx-4 flex items-center gap-2 overflow-x-auto px-4 [scrollbar-width:none] [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden sm:mx-0 sm:justify-center sm:gap-4 sm:overflow-visible sm:px-0">
and render `{idx > 0 && <ChevronRight className="h-5 w-5 shrink-0 text-primary-200" />}` as a direct child of that flex row rather than inside the per-chip wrapper at line 560. For the mobile clip, add a right-edge fade so the cut is legible as 'there is more': wrap the scroller in `<div className="relative after:pointer-events-none after:absolute after:inset-y-0 after:right-0 after:w-8 after:bg-gradient-to-l after:from-card sm:after:hidden">`. Finally, either define `.no-scrollbar` once in globals-components-layout.css or delete all three usages — right now it is a lie in three files.

title: On every marketing page the hero sits 128px inboard of every section below it — max-w-5xl hero against max-w-7xl sections
evidence: Hero container is `mx-auto max-w-5xl px-4 … lg:px-8` (pricing/page.tsx:78) = 1024px cap; at 1440 its content edge is (1440−1024)/2 + 32 = 240px. MarketingSection (marketing-section.tsx:34) is `mx-auto w-full max-w-7xl px-4 … lg:px-8` = 1280px cap; its content edge is (1440−1280)/2 + 32 = 112px. Difference = 128px. Confirmed by opening pricing__w1440__light.png: the hero eyebrow 'ค่าธรรมเนียม' and the H1 begin at x≈240, while every section eyebrow below — 'รายละเอียด', 'ช่องทางชำระเงิน', 'เงื่อนไขสัญญา' — begins at x≈112. pricing__w390__light.png shows them aligned, because below 1024px both containers fall back to px-4/px-6 and the caps never bind.
why_it_matters: Scrolling a public government fee schedule, the page visibly shifts its left margin once, right after the headline. A grid that does not hold is the fastest way for a page to read as assembled rather than designed, and it is on the four pages a citizen reads before deciding whether to trust the platform with money.
fix:
Give the heroes the same container as the sections. In each of pricing/page.tsx:78, about/page.tsx:61, terms-of-service/page.tsx:134 and privacy-policy/page.tsx:174:
- <div className="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-4 py-14 sm:px-6 md:py-20 lg:px-8">
+ <div className="mx-auto w-full max-w-7xl px-4 py-14 sm:px-6 md:py-20 lg:px-8">
The hero's own reading measure is already protected separately by `max-w-3xl` on the paragraph (pricing/page.tsx:85), so widening the container does not stretch the copy. Better still: export the container from marketing-section.tsx as `<MarketingContainer>` and use it in both places so the two can never drift again.

title: The button size scale tops out below Apple's 44pt touch minimum, so 223 places hard-code h-[44px]/w-[44px] to escape it — while four sub-32px sizes remain on offer
evidence: button.tsx:37-44 defines sm: h-9 (36px), md: h-10 (40px), lg: h-11 (44px), icon: h-10 w-10 (40px), compact-xs: h-6 (24px), compact-sm: h-7 (28px), compact-md: h-8 (32px), xs: h-7 (28px). defaultVariants at :47-50 is size 'md' = 40px. Counted usages across src/**/*.tsx: size="sm" 233, size="lg" 31, size="md" 19, size="xs" 15, size="compact-xs" 11, size="compact-sm" 4, size="icon" 2. So the dominant control in the app is 36px tall and the default is 40px — both under 44. Meanwhile the codebase contains 156 occurrences of the arbitrary class `h-[44px]` and 67 of `w-[44px]` (grep of arbitrary bracket classes: these are the #1 and #4 most common of 906 total), i.e. 223 hand-written escapes reaching for a value the named scale will not give them except under the name 'lg'. For contrast, the mobile bottom nav was done right — globals-components-layout.css:301-315 sets `min-height: 44px` on .gov-bottom-nav-item.
why_it_matters: The users are farmers filling forms outdoors on a phone, often one-handed. Every 36px control is a target they will miss some of the time, and the 24-28px compact sizes are barely half the minimum. The 223 arbitrary escapes are the design system telling you it is wrong: engineers already know 44 is the right number and are routing around the tokens to get it.
fix:
Reset the scale so the names carry the right values on touch and the compact sizes cannot be used for primary actions. In button.tsx:37-44:
  sm: 'h-11 px-4 md:h-9 md:px-3',
  md: 'h-11 px-5 md:h-10 md:px-4',
  lg: 'h-12 px-6 md:h-11 md:px-5',
  icon: 'h-11 w-11 md:h-10 md:w-10',
Keep compact-xs/compact-sm/compact-md but rename them to make their scope explicit (e.g. 'table-xs') and add an ESLint rule that rejects them outside dense table cells. Then codemod the 223 `h-[44px]`/`w-[44px]` sites to `h-11`/`w-11` and add a lint rule banning arbitrary height values on interactive elements — if a value is needed often enough to appear 156 times, it belongs in the scale.

title: Five competing card surfaces, nine distinct radii (two of them the same number under different names), and 9:1 stock-Tailwind shadows over design tokens — one of which is declared and never used
where: apps/web-app/src/components/ui/primitives/card.tsx:10; apps/web-app/src/styles/globals-components-layout.css:1-9, :96-102, :116-117; apps/web-app/tailwind.config.cjs boxShadow block and borderRadius override
evidence: Counted across src/**/*.tsx. RADII: rounded (4px) 153, rounded-sm (2px) 1, rounded-md (6px) 158, rounded-lg 743, rounded-xl 425, rounded-2xl (16px) 193, rounded-3xl (24px) 2, rounded-full 260, rounded-[1.375rem] (22px) 43, rounded-[2rem] (32px) 4 — and note tailwind.config.cjs overrides borderRadius.lg to `var(--radius)` = 0.75rem (globals.css:47), which is 12px, i.e. `rounded-lg` and `rounded-xl` are the SAME value under two names across 1,168 usages. SURFACES: `Card` primitive = rounded-[1.375rem] + shadow-leaf-card (card.tsx:10, 385 usages); `.surface-card` = rounded-3xl + --shadow-md (layout.css:1-4); `.surface-panel` = rounded-2xl + --shadow-sm (:6-9); `.form-panel` = rounded-3xl + shadow-md (:96-98); ad-hoc `rounded-lg bg-card … shadow-sm` 88 usages. `.field-emphasis` then forces `border-radius: 0.75rem !important` (:117) on every input, select, textarea and date field, so a field can never match its card by design. SHADOWS: stock Tailwind shadow-sm 248, shadow-xl 31, shadow-md 30, shadow-lg 30, shadow-2xl 9, shadow-inner 4 = 352, against the six declared tokens shadow-leaf-card 20, shadow-leaf-btn 8, shadow-card 8, shadow-leaf-card-hover 2, shadow-officer-btn 1, shadow-soft 0 = 39. `shadow-soft` is declared in tailwind.config.cjs and used zero times. Visually: health_applications__w390__light.png cards read visibly rounder than health_training__w390__light.png cards (22-24px vs 12px), and health_establishments_new__w390__light.png shows three radii in one glance — 22px card, 12px fields, fully-pill buttons.
why_it_matters: Radius and shadow are how a surface tells you what kind of thing it is. Right now the same concept — 'a card' — is drawn five ways, so the eye cannot learn the language. The tell is `rounded-lg`/`rounded-xl` resolving to one number: nobody could have chosen both on purpose, which means these classes are being typed from habit rather than from a decision.
fix: Pick three radii and delete the rest: 12px for controls and fields (--radius, already the value), 22px for cards (--radius-card: 1.375rem), 9999px for pills. Then (a) stop overriding borderRadius.lg in tailwind.config.cjs so `rounded-lg` means 8px again and codemod today's `rounded-lg` on card surfaces to `rounded-card`; (b) collapse .surface-card / .surface-panel / .form-panel into the Card primitive with a `tone` prop and delete them from globals-components-layout.css; (c) codemod the 88 `rounded-lg bg-card … shadow-sm` sites to `<Card>`; (d) remove `border-radius: … !important` from .field-emphasis:117 so fields inherit the control radius; (e) delete the unused `soft` shadow from tailwind.config.cjs and add an ESLint rule rejecting raw shadow-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl outside the primitives directory, which is what turns this from a cleanup into a rule.

title: Desktop is the un-designed viewport: the mobile column is stretched to 1440 rather than composed for it
evidence: Opened trace_960853e6_7c3d_461d_a62a_1fb96e687a2d__w1440__light.png: the entire public verification page is a 288px column (max-w-xs 320px minus px-4, lines 127 and 167) centred in 1440px, with 576px of empty mint on each side — a phone screenshot pinned to a desktop wall. Opened health_profile__w1440__light.png: each of the six navigation rows is 1216px wide with its label at x=180 and its chevron at x=1300, and each info row puts a 60px label above a 200px value in a 1216px box. Opened health_establishments_new__w1440__light.png: the single-line farm-name input spans x=128 to x=1312 — a 1184px text field for a farm name, while the จังหวัด/อำเภอ/ตำบล row directly below correctly uses three columns. Opened health_dashboard__w1440__light.png: content ends at y≈670 with roughly 400px of empty background before the footer, and the six action cards are 630px wide holding a 40px icon and two short lines each. All four routes report horizOverflow=false and CLS under 0.01, so nothing is broken — the space is simply not composed.
why_it_matters: DTAM officers and many farmers work at a desk. Right now the desktop experience is the mobile experience with air added: a 1184px input invites a 20-character answer, a chevron 1120px from its label breaks the visual bond between a row and its affordance, and the QR page — the platform's public face — looks unfinished on the machine a journalist or a buyer's compliance officer will open it on. This is the difference between working and being worth looking at.
fix: Three concrete moves. (1) trace/[qr-code]/client-view.tsx:127 and :167 — go two-column above lg: `lg:max-w-4xl` on the wrapper at :167 and `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,380px)_minmax(0,1fr)] lg:gap-6` on the inner stack at :168, putting the identity card and lab result in the left rail and the timeline in the right; keep the single column below lg. (2) Constrain form measure: give the establishments form's full-width rows `max-w-xl` (a farm name never needs more than ~576px) and let only the address textarea run to `max-w-3xl` — or better, put the whole form in a `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-2 lg:gap-x-8` and let the address span both. (3) On /health/profile, cap the settings list at `max-w-2xl` and left-align it under the header, or make the six rows a `md:grid-cols-2` card grid — either kills the 1120px chevron gap. Same treatment for the dashboard's six action cards: `xl:grid-cols-3` instead of two, which also removes most of the 400px dead zone above the footer.
